_source: Every note in this file was written for this room. WHAT each site is was read off that site's own pages -- Star Stuff's about page, Cavendish Space's origin page, the Map of Monotropic Experiences' own front page, the Why Sheet Press's own repository -- and where a site describes itself in a phrase worth keeping, the phrase is attributed to it rather than absorbed. Nothing here was written from memory, and nothing here is lifted from data/arrivals.json's notes: The Feed says what has arrived from a site and this says what grows there, and two rooms holding one paragraph is one room with two doors.
_roster: WHICH SITES ARE IN THE GARDEN IS NOT DECIDED HERE. make-garden.py reads the roster and the running order out of data/arrivals.json, whose own order is stimpunks.org's published feeds page -- the one place our sites are collected by somebody deciding. So a bed cannot be invented here, a site cannot be quietly left out, and re-sorting the garden would mean overruling a decision made somewhere else, which is the rule the Jungle Room keeps about its cams. A wire with no bed is refused; a bed with no wire is refused.
_itself: THIS STREET IS A BED IN ITS OWN GARDEN, for The Feed's reason: a garden that listed every bed and left out the one under your feet would be claiming to be the gardener rather than a plant.
_forms: Each bed's drawing is a different HABIT OF GROWTH, and the habit is the argument -- which is why every one of them is also written out in words on the page. The drawings are aria-hidden decoration, and a picture carrying a claim that only sighted readers get is not a claim this site is allowed to make. make-garden.py refuses a bed with no habit sentence and two beds that share a drawing.
_no_counts: NO BED SAYS HOW MUCH A SITE HOLDS. Not the number of glossary terms, not the number of sheets, not how many zines are out. Two reasons and either is enough: a number like that is wrong within the week and authoritative-looking in the meantime, which is the fault The Feed avoids by publishing the minute it was read; and a garden measured by volume is an inventory. Cite the thing, not the size of it. make-garden.py refuses the pattern.
_no_ranking: No bed is bigger, better, busier or more important than another, and the tool refuses the vocabulary with the negation window make-guild.py uses, so the room can still say that it does not rank anything. stimpunks.org is described as the one the others were built to take weight off, which is a fact about how they came to exist rather than a league table.
_no_dates: AND NO BED CARRIES A DATE, which is what keeps this room out of The Feed. That board is a timetable -- a title, a date, a destination, and the minute it was set. This is a planting plan: what a site is for, whose hands are in it, and nothing that changes when somebody publishes. So this tool needs no network and has no pull step, and it refuses a date in a bed's copy rather than trusting nobody to add one.
_links: A NOTE MAY ONLY POINT AT ITS OWN PLANT. Every link inside a bed's `what` has to be one of our own pages or somewhere on that bed's own host, refused otherwise -- make-hermitage.py's rule about the Star Stuff table, where a bench with somebody's name on it holding something else reads as a claim. The `with` line is the exception and is the whole reason it exists: that is where a collaborator's name and a collaborator's own site go.

stimpunks.what: The garden itself, and the one the others were built to take weight off: a glossary kept in public, a pattern language grown out of lived experience, recipes for the environments those patterns ask for, and the frameworks that came out of all three. Its own page about the garden says nothing there needs to be read in order, and means it.
stimpunks.habit: A rhizome, running sideways under the bed and coming up in several places at once. That is the shape our own page gives this knowledge, and Autistic Rhizome is a term in the glossary it comes up in.
stimpunks.with: Stimpunks Foundation, and everybody whose writing the glossary credits by name.

starstuff.what: Zines, field guides and broadsides that start from something settled in physics, cosmology, chemistry or biology and let it carry an argument about belonging — not as loose metaphor, but as the same pattern showing up at more than one scale. Its about page calls itself the public flowering of this garden, which is its phrase and not ours.
starstuff.habit: An umbel coming into flower: one stem, and every ray of it opening at the same height. It is the bed in flower because that site said it was.
starstuff.with: A collaboration between Stimpunks and More Realms, where a great deal of it was grown from seed.

queering.what: A cabinet of mounted sheets on queerness, illness and the natural world, with an accession register that publishes its own corrections rather than quietly fixing them. One of the sheets in it is about Monotropa uniflora, the ghost pipe, which makes no chlorophyll of its own and lives by what it is connected to underground.
queering.habit: That plant, which is why this is the one bed in the garden with no green in it at all. It is carried by its outline and by the threads running out of it, the way the things in it are.
queering.with: Built with Helen Edgar of Autistic Realms, who is named on the sheets she wrote rather than folded into our “we”, and with contributions credited on the cabinet's own pages.

cavendish.what: Caves, campfires, watering holes, the library of what we have worked out, and the habitat that holds all four — plus the Cavendish Cards deck, which lets somebody point at a picture instead of explaining, and the room sheets for working out which zones a real room can already hold. Everything there is free and CC0.
cavendish.habit: The one bed with something built over it, because that site is about the structure: a frame changes what a bed can grow, which is the whole argument for zoning a room rather than telling somebody to cope in it.
cavendish.with: Stimpunks Foundation. The three primordial spaces are David Thornburg's, from From the Campfire to the Holodeck; the name comes from Henry Cavendish by way of Steve Silberman's NeuroTribes; and Ira Socol's home of opportunity is on that site's origin page beside them.

pebbling.what: A card game about bringing somebody a small thing for no reason, and about what that does. No winners, no pressure to perform, and you can leave whenever you need to. There is a cabinet in our arcade built on the same practice that deliberately takes nothing from that deck — the deck is the better thing and it is here.
pebbling.habit: Runners: the plant reaches sideways and puts a new plant down beside itself, roots and all, without being asked for anything back. That is pebbling rather than trading.
pebbling.with: Helen Edgar of Autistic Realms and Ryan Boren of Stimpunks, together. The locution the practice is described in is Amythest Schaber's.

whysheet.what: One-page arguments, openly licensed and editable, made to be printed and carried into a room where somebody is about to be talked over. You tick the sheets you need and the press hands back a single correctly paginated PDF with the citations intact. Nothing is uploaded and no account is kept.
whysheet.habit: A seed head gone dry, which is the only bed here whose point is that you take it away. What it grows into somewhere we will never see is the intended outcome rather than a side effect.
whysheet.with: Stimpunks Foundation, and the researchers, lawyers and self-advocates each sheet cites on its own face.

love.what: The street you are standing on, and the loud half of the same lung. No single design system, no two rooms alike, credits scrawled in the margins, and a dial that lets you decide how much of it happens. The street is that way and the liner notes say where everything in it came from.
love.habit: A scramble: nasturtiums over the edges of the bed, out onto the path and up whatever is standing near them. Nothing in this bed has been kept in its row.
love.with: Stimpunks Foundation, with a pitch in the campgrounds that is Helen Edgar's own room and a community board kept by Norah Hobbs.

monotropic.what: Twenty places a monotropic person goes, drawn as an island you can walk — attention tunnels, rabbit holes of research, infodump canyon, burnout whirlpools, the forest of joy, awe and wonder — with a second tool for drawing your own. Some of those places are where the good work happens and some are weather that other people make.
monotropic.habit: A tendril: the stem puts out a feeler, finds something, and holds on. Tendril Theory is one of the places on that island, which is why this bed grows the thing the theory is named after.
monotropic.with: Helen Edgar's map of her own Autistic and ADHD experience, published with Stimpunks. Monotropism is Dinah Murray, Wenn Lawson and Mike Lesser's.

_next_door: AUTISTIC REALMS AND MORE REALMS ARE NOT BEDS AND CANNOT BE. A bed is a site we publish, and the roster for that is data/arrivals.json, whose order is stimpunks.org's own feeds page. These are Helen Edgar's own sites, tended by her, and the only way to make them beds would have been to write them into that roster -- which would put them on The Feed as our wires and claim somebody else's work as ours in the one file this room is not allowed to invent. So they are through the ivy instead: named, linked, said out loud to be hers, and drawn as something seen from this side rather than something growing in our ground. make-garden.py refuses a plot that IS on the roster, for the same reason it refuses a bed that is not.
_no_ground: AND YOU CANNOT SEE THEIR GROUND. Every bed's drawing shows the soil and most of them show what is under it; a plot's drawing stops where the ivy runs, and the tool refuses a coordinate past that line. We do not get to draw the roots of somebody else's garden. It is also why nothing over there casts a shadow: the sun is still overhead in this room, but the floor a shadow would land on is on the far side of the ivy.
_cuttings: EVERY PLOT SAYS WHAT OF IT IS ALREADY IN THIS GARDEN, and the tool refuses one that does not. Without that line this section is a list of a friend's websites on a page about ours. With it, it is the other half of every `with` line in the beds above: those say who helped us, and this says whose garden that help walked out of. The direction of the credit is the whole point, which is why it is a field rather than a nicety.

autisticrealms.what: Helen Edgar's own site, and the grounded one: neuro-affirming resources, reading lists, glossaries of the language to use and the language to avoid, and signposting for families, educators and Autistic people who have arrived without the words yet. Her own page sets out what the work is for as being, belonging and becoming, in that order, and she writes as an Autistic advocate, author and consultant who spent twenty years teaching in SEND early years and primary settings before any of this. Monotropism, flow and burnout are where she goes deepest.
autisticrealms.habit: A nurse tree, which is planted to take the weather off whatever is growing under it until that can stand in its own light. The shelter is the work and it is not the same work as the growing — which is her argument rather than our metaphor: her page says young Autistic people need to feel accepted and understood first, and that the conditions come before the flourishing.
autisticrealms.whose: Helen Edgar, who is a colleague and not a corpus. Her site is hers, her name is on her own writing there, and nothing of hers is folded into our “we” on this street either.
autisticrealms.here: She built Queering.Earth with us and is named on the sheets she wrote; Penguin Pebbling is hers and Ryan Boren's together; the Map of Monotropic Experiences is her own map of her own Autistic and ADHD experience, published with us. There is a yurt pitched in our campgrounds that is her room rather than ours, down to the colours.

morerealms.what: The wilder ground past it, and hers as well. Its own landing page says you have arrived beyond Autistic Realms and that things here are “looser, weirder, more speculative” — not a place of conclusions or answers but somewhere to wander, think sideways and dwell. Spiral time, liminal embodiment, neuroqueer and post-humanist reading, written monotropically. Its phrase and not ours: “there is no map, but there are threads, glimmers, and soft, weird spaces to explore”.
morerealms.habit: A fern's crozier, still coiled. It opens from the inside outwards, slowly, and is the only thing in either garden that grows by unwinding rather than by reaching. Spiral time is that site's own phrase for how it moves, and a frond keeps the turn in it long after it has opened.
morerealms.whose: Helen Edgar again — one gardener, and this is the plot she keeps for the work that does not have to arrive anywhere.
morerealms.here: Star Stuff and Queering.Earth are both Stimpunks and More Realms, which is how her own pages about them describe the arrangement — a collaboration between Helen Edgar and Ryan Boren — rather than how we have decided to describe it here.

_the_ivy: THE BOUNDARY SHIPPED AS A WOVEN FENCE AND IS IVY BECAUSE HELEN ASKED -- her call, 2026-09-22, on a drawing of her own gardens. She was right about more than the picture: A FENCE SAYS KEPT OUT AND IVY SAYS THIS IS AS FAR AS WE CAN SEE. What that line marks is the edge of what WE know and never the edge of where anybody may go, which is the opposite reading and the correct one on a page about somebody else's work. It is recorded here, in make-garden.py, in the room, in the changelog and in the liner notes, for the reason the one colour of hers this repository ever changed is recorded in four places -- except that this correction runs the other way, from a contributor to us, which is worth writing down at least as loudly. She asked for stars with it and THEY ARE GLIMMERS RATHER THAN A SKY: this room is midday and stays midday, nothing is lit by them, and nothing ambient was added to the page, so the street's one daylit garden is not quietly turned into a night one. `Threads, glimmers, and soft, weird spaces` is More Realms' own line about itself and is where the word comes from. Do not finish them into a starfield, and do not put the fence back.
